subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should OpenAI cache-TTL pruning be enabled through the existing provider eligibility gate, or should this issue wait for a provider-agnostic/retention-aware pruning mode?
rationale: Current main proves the reported gate is real, but changing it activates pruning for existing OpenAI configurations and intersects OpenAI prompt-cache retention policy, so automation should not choose the product semantics alone.

options.title: Review and harden the linked OpenAI eligibility PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95859 as the active candidate, require maintainer-approved OpenAI TTL semantics, and ask for redacted native OpenAI idle-gap proof before merge.

options.title: Accept the direct eligibility change as intentional
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept that existing OpenAI cache-ttl configs become active with the current TTL behavior, then land a narrow eligibility/test change with proof.

options.title: Pause for provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: If cache-TTL eligibility is the wrong abstraction for OpenAI, keep this issue open and close/replace the current PR in favor of a new pruning mode or policy.

recommendation.title: Review and harden the linked OpenAI eligibility PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95859 as the active candidate, require maintainer-approved OpenAI TTL semantics, and ask for redacted native OpenAI idle-gap proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current helper/factory blame and recent prompt-cache sync history route the implementation surface most directly to vincentkoc.
